title: Reading Corner Newsletter on Decoding Skills
source_title: Kramer Elementary | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
Title 

Talk 

Title Talk

Title Talk Reading Corner February NewsletterWhat does decoding mean? A simple definition for decoding is recognizing letter sounds or patterns and blending them together to translate a written word into speech. Decoding is a foundational reading skill (phonics) that must be developed to begin successful reading with fluency. This process begins with students recognizing their letters and sounds then blending the sounds to speak the word, i.e., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ becomes cat.Here is an example of what happens when a student decodes a word:Recognizing letters and letter patterns (like b, sh, igh)Knowing the sounds they makeBlending those sounds together to read a wordActivities: Reading Rockets is a reputable research-based website for all things reading; and below are age-specific resources for decoding activities.Kindergarten: https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101Kindergartener phonics and decoding activitiesFirst Grade:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-first-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activitiesSecond Grade:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-second-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activitiesThird Grade:Here is a video showing how a 3rd grade student uses syllables to decode longer words more easily.Questions or need help? Please reach out to your child's Reading Corner instructor; Mrs. Geshan, geshanc@talawanda.org, Mrs. Kobermann, kobermanc@talawanda.org, or Mrs. Walters, waltersh@talawanda.org.

summary: The February **Reading Corner Newsletter** explains decoding—the foundational reading skill of recognizing letter sounds and blending them to read words. The newsletter provides **grade-specific decoding activities** for Kindergarten through 3rd grade via Reading Rockets website links, including a video showing how 3rd graders use syllables to decode longer words. Parents can contact Mrs. Geshan (geshanc@talawanda.org), Mrs. Kobermann (kobermanc@talawanda.org), or Mrs. Walters (waltersh@talawanda.org) with questions.

title: Office Notes: Fees, Lunch Accounts, and Dismissal
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
NOTES 

FROM 

THE 

OFFICE

NOTES FROM THE OFFICE

zoom_out_map
            
Student Fees:Fees have been loaded to PaySchools if you wish to pay online. You can also pay in the office with cash or check.Lunch Accounts:As a reminder, you are able to add funds to your student's lunch account through the PaySchools system. If your student's account reaches -$50 it will be rolled into your school fees. Please be mindful and keep your student's account current. You can use PaySchools, send a check or cash to the school office to take care of your student's balance.Free and Reduced:If you would like to apply for free or reduced lunches, please reach out to the Marshall office or the Marshall social worker Chrissy Rolfes at rolfesc@talawanda.org. We can help walk you through the online application or help you fill out a paper form in the office. If you qualify for FREE lunch, your fees will also be waived. (EXCEPT for 5th grade Chromebook fee) If you qualify for REDUCED, fees will be reduced by 85% (EXCEPT for 5th grade Chromebook fee) and meals will be FREE.Dismissal:Thank you for your help in keeping dismissal safe and smooth for everyone. We ask that when your child is called to your car, you please help them climb in and then pull forward to the upper lot to buckle them into their car seat. Remaining stopped in the dismissal lane to buckle your child slows down the process for all families and, more importantly, it creates an unsafe situation when other cars attempt to go around. Your cooperation makes dismissal safer and quicker for all of our students.Final Forms:Remember, if you have any changes to your information (phone number, address, who can pick up your student, etc) throughout the school year, change it in Final Forms! The office is notified of these changes and will update our information. IF you have an address change, you must submit new proof of residency to the office before we will update your address.

summary: **Student fees** are now available to pay online through PaySchools or in the office with cash/check. **Lunch accounts** can be funded through PaySchools; accounts reaching -$50 will roll into school fees. Families can apply for **free/reduced lunch** by contacting the Marshall office or social worker Chrissy Rolfes at rolfesc@talawanda.org—qualifying families receive fee waivers or 85% reduction (except 5th grade Chromebook fee). At **dismissal**, please pull forward to the upper lot to buckle children after they enter your car to keep the process safe and efficient. Update any contact or address changes through **Final Forms** (address changes require new proof of residency submitted to the office).
